names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 27 iulie, «Sfântul Mare Mucenic și Tămăduitor Pantelimon», with the rank words left off.

The name he bore before his martyrdom, as the same page gives it: «Ο Άγιος Παντελεήμων (Παντελέων το πρότερον όνομα)». The page says a voice from heaven at his beheading called him no longer Παντελέων but Παντελεήμων, which is the form the folder already holds.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 27. јул ст. ст., „Свeти великомученик Пантелејмон.“, with the heading’s first word — which is “saint” and no rank, and which this page misspells with a Latin e — and «великомученик», the rank, left off by §6. **The stored FORM is clean Cyrillic**; it is the attestation’s quoted `text` that carries the page’s mixed-script heading, because §4 quotes a heading and §6 stores a name, and those are two different obligations. `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM`, so the bare forename costs nothing. The Serbian vernacular differs from the Greek Παντελεήμων, the Russian Пантелеимон and the Romanian Pantelimon this folder already holds, and nothing is transliterated.

death.note: The year printed beside his name on days.pravoslavie.ru for 27 July (old style).

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 27 июля ст. ст. — «Вмч. и целителя Пантелеимона (305)»
Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 27 iulie — «Sfântul Mare Mucenic și Tămăduitor Pantelimon»

attestations.note: doxologia.ro's life under that line is this man's: «Intre aceștia a pătimit pentru Hristos și Sfântul Mare Mucenic Pantelimon, din cetatea Nicomidiei, care se află în părțile Bitiniei… din tată de neam bun, cinstit și bogat, cu numele Evstorghie și din maica sa, Euvula», under Maximian. Read 24 September 2026. The site's troparion page for him is an audio recording with no printed text, so no Romanian hymn is added.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 27ης Ιουλίου — «Άγιος Παντελεήμων ο Μεγαλομάρτυς και Ιαματικός»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 27 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries and the same menologion day as its Russian row; the Greek calendar reckons in revised-julian, so its 27 July is the civil day. The man is the folder's own: «Αγιος Παντελεημων ο Μεγαλομαρτυς Και Ιαματικος (; - 305)», of Nicomedia, physician, great-martyr and healer, and the folder's existing `greek` name form «Παντελεήμων» came from this calendar already. The Greek page adds a great deal the folder did not have: his earlier name Παντελέων, his father Eustorgios the pagan whom his son's admonitions made a Christian, his mother Euboule whom the same calendar keeps on 30 Μαρτίου, Euphrosynos who trained him in medicine, the priest Hermolaus of Nicomedia who catechised and baptised him and whom the same calendar keeps on 26 Ιουλίου, the raising of the young man killed by a viper, the voice from heaven that called him not Panteleon but Panteleimon, the sword that bent and the iron that melted like wax, the soldiers who became Christians at the sight, the milk instead of blood and the olive tree that suddenly bore fruit. It also names Florina and Tilos as the towns that keep him as patron. The year on the head line, 305, and the reign of Maximian it dates «(286 - 305 μ.Χ.)» agree with the folder's existing `dates`, which are therefore not touched. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints an apolytikion and a kontakion, both of which name him and both of which are taken, and also a μεγαλυνάριον, an οἶκος and a κάθισμα, which the schema's `kind` enum cannot hold and which are therefore not drafted.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 09.08.2026 (27. јул ст. ст.) — „Свeти великомученик Пантелејмон.“

attestations.note: The day’s first and longest entry, quoted whole with its closing full stop (§4) — **and the quotation carries a defect of the page that a reader must not mend.** The heading as the Prologue’s own `<strong>` element prints it is „Свeти великомученик Пантелејмон.“, in which the first word is spelt with a **LATIN e** inside the Cyrillic: `Св` then U+0065 then `ти`, where every other heading of this range has «Свети» with U+0435. It is the page’s own letter, §4 says quote the heading whole, and a reader does not repair a source — so the mixed-script string is what the attestation `text` carries, and **it will not match a search for the Cyrillic spelling**, which is said here so that nobody later reads it as a transcription error of this batch. `types` UNTOUCHED, AND ALL THREE ARE CORROBORATED. «великомученик» is the `great-martyr` this folder carries; `physician` is confirmed by „Као младић изучио лекарске науке. Свештеник Ермолај призва га к себи, научи га вери Христовој и крсти га.“, as a young man he learned the physician’s sciences; and `unmercenary` is confirmed by the entry’s closing note on the services — „Св. Пантелејмон призива се у молитвама при водоосвећењу и јелеосвећењу (свештању масла) заједно са св. Ермолајем и осталим безсребреницима и чудотворцима.“, Saint Panteleimon is called on at the blessing of water and of oil **together with Saint Hermolaus and the other UNMERCENARIES and wonderworkers**. A type already held is not written twice. **THE DATE IS REFUSED, AND IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS YESTERDAY’S ON THE SAME COMPANY OF MEN.** The folder holds `death` 305/305, display «305», basis traditional. This entry states „Чесно пострада за Христа овај дивни мученик у младости својој 27. јула 304. год.“ — he suffered in his youth **on the 27 July in the year 304**. A second point, one year off the first, in a field that is not empty: writing it would displace a recorded year. **And the pairing is worth the line**: the Julian 26 July gave «около 304» for Hermolaus, whose folder also holds 305, so **this book says 304 for both men of one martyrdom and this corpus holds 305 for both**, which makes it one disagreement between two books and not two. The one-line alternative is named in this batch’s commit message. **TWO FOLDERS THAT EXIST, ARE KEPT ON THIS VERY DAY, AND GET NO ROW BY §5 — THE SECOND AND THIRD SUCH CASE IN TWO DAYS.** „Чудотворно излечи Пантелејмон једнога слепца, кога су други лекари узалуд лечили; излечи га именом Христовим, и крсти га.“ — Panteleimon healed **a certain blind man** whom other physicians had treated in vain, and baptised him. `blind-man-healed-by-panteleimon` is a folder of this corpus, is kept on the Julian 27/7, holds NO name form in any language, and its `serbian` row stands `undocumented`. **It gets nothing**: the man is narrated in this body and the heading does not name him — it could not, the book giving him no name either. And „Тада и св. Ермолај са Ермипом и Ермократом пострада.“, then Hermolaus too suffered with Hermippus and Hermocrates: all three are folders, all three are on this menologion number, **and `hermolaus-of-nicomedia` took his `serbian` row yesterday on the Julian 26 July, which is his own day in this book.** A row here would be a second Serbian day for him and §5 refuses it before the question arises. `hermippus-of-nicomedia` and `hermocrates-of-nicomedia` are refused for the second day running, on the same ground. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS. „Родом из Никомидије од мајке хришћанке и оца незнабошца. Мајка му се звала Евула а отац Евсторгије.“ — **his mother was called Евула and his father Евсторгије**, a Christian mother and a heathen father. „Као младић изучио лекарске науке. Свештеник Ермолај призва га к себи, научи га вери Христовој и крсти га.“, the priest Hermolaus called him, taught him and baptised him. „Из зависти оптуже лекари Пантелејмона као хришћанина, и Пантелејмон изађе пред цара Максимијана на суд.“, the physicians accused him out of envy. **AND THEN THE ONE SENTENCE OF THIS DAY THE BOOK ITSELF PUTS IN QUOTATION MARKS**: „„И стаде пред земаљским царем телом, а умом стајаше пред Царем небеским.““ — and he stood before the earthly emperor in body, but in mind he stood before the heavenly King. „Пред царем он се слободно објави хришћанином, и на очи цареве излечи једног узетог човека од дуготрајне болести. Ово чудо многе незнабошце привуче вери Христовој.“, he healed a paralysed man before the emperor’s own eyes and drew many of the heathen. „Цар га стави на муке, но Господ му се јави у неколико махова и избави га цела и неповређена.“, the Lord appeared to him several times in his torments and delivered him whole. „Осуђен на смрт св. Пантелејмон клече на молитву. У том џелат удари га мачем по врату, и мач се преби као да је од воска.“ — **the executioner struck his neck and the SWORD BROKE AS THOUGH IT WERE OF WAX**; „И не могаше га џелат погубити док светитељ не сврши молитву и сам не рече да га посеку.“, and the executioner could not kill him until the saint had finished his prayer and himself told them to strike. „Његове мошти посташе целебне. Беше посечен Пантелејмон под неком маслином, која по том постаде сва окићена плодом.“ — **he was beheaded under an olive tree WHICH AFTERWARDS BECAME ALL DECKED WITH FRUIT**. „Пантелејмон – значи свемилостиви. Бог свемилостиви прими праведну душу његову, и прослави га међу великим светитељима својим.“, and the entry glosses his name: **Panteleimon means all-merciful, and the all-merciful God received his soul**. „Најдивнији храм, посвећен овом светитељу налази се у Светој Гори.“, the most wonderful church dedicated to him is on the Holy Mountain. **NO NEW `related`, AND FOUR PARTIES TAKE NONE.** `hermolaus-of-nicomedia`, `euboula-mother-of-panteleimon` and `blind-man-healed-by-panteleimon` are all three already on this folder, and `proseprobe.mjs` reported Hermolaus **OK** before the paragraph was written. **THE FATHER Евсторгије HOLDS NO FOLDER**: `ls saints | grep -i eustorgi` returns nothing at all. **THE EMPEROR MAXIMIAN IS A PERSECUTOR AND NOBODY’S SAINT**, and the executioner, the envious physicians and the paralysed man are named by no name. **THE CHURCH ON THE HOLY MOUNTAIN IS A DEDICATION.** No `office`. No `locations`: Nicomedia and the Holy Mountain are named and neither is written as a coordinate. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Ἀθλοφόρε Ἅγιε, καὶ ἰαματικὲ Παντελεῆμον, πρέσβευε τῷ ἐλεήμονι Θεῷ, ἵνα πταισμάτων ἄφεσιν, παράσχῃ ταῖς ψυχαῖς ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος γ’ — on the page of «Άγιος Παντελεήμων ο Μεγαλομάρτυς και Ιαματικός». It names him with his byname of healer, so it is his own proper; the page names no automelon for it

english.text: Holy prize-winner and healer Panteleimon, intercede with the merciful God, that he may grant our souls the forgiveness of their offences.

hymns.text: Μιμητὴς ὑπάρχων τοῦ ἐλεήμονος, καὶ ἰαμάτων τὴν χάριν παρ᾽αὐτοῦ κομισάμενος, ἀθλοφόρε καὶ Μάρτυς Χριστοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ, ταῖς εὐχαῖς σου τὰς ψυχικὰς ἡμῶν νόσους θεράπευσον, ἀπελαύνων τοῦ ἀεί, πολεμίου τὰ σκάνδαλα, ἐκ τῶν βοώντων ἀπαύστως· Σῶσον ἡμᾶς Κύριε.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος πλ. α’ — the second hymn on the page of «Άγιος Παντελεήμων ο Μεγαλομάρτυς και Ιαματικός». It turns on his name, the imitator of the Merciful One, and on his gift of healings, so it is his own proper

english.text: Being an imitator of the Merciful One and having received from him the grace of healings, prize-winner and martyr of Christ our God, heal by your prayers the sicknesses of our souls, driving off the stumbling-blocks of the everlasting enemy from those who cry out unceasingly: save us, O Lord.
